title: Opt-in code mode off and on, current gateway models, with fan_out
note: Supersedes 2026-10-19-codemode, which reached three of seven models because the gateway had stopped serving the other four. Both arms run the same bake-rs build of b3bcb94a9c; on adds codemode to defaultTools, where it is opt-in. The models are the newest of each lab the gateway serves, plus DeepSeek two through its own API. kimi-k2.7-code reaches the gateway only from 7281a9694f, which gives the Chat Completions families the system role; before it every Kimi request failed with 400 "role developer is not allowed", so it has no earlier pair. The scenarios are the standard suite and fan_out, new here. Accepted regressions: total tokens on claude-sonnet-5 (+36.5%), deepseek-v4-pro (+27.1%), gpt-6-sol (+20.0%), and deepseek-flash (+17.8%). Offering codemode adds about 2.1 KB of tool definitions to every request (toolSchemaChars 4692-4860 to 6823-7004). Only claude-opus-5 (29 calls in 16 of 27 samples) and gpt-6-sol (24 calls in 15 of 27) chose it. The other six never did, so their rises are the definition alone. Opus batched reads and edits in scripts: requests -11.8%, tool calls 109 to 68, tokens -6.7% with an interval that spans zero. gpt-6-sol cut requests 11.3% and tool calls 106 to 78, but its scripts return whole outputs, so the fewer round trips carry more tokens. On fan_out with codemode merely offered, the models summed the ledgers with a shell command. Only gpt-6-sol fanned out reads inside a script, and only twice: one script read all sixteen ledgers. The paired codemode-only-fan-out record measures fan_out when the model must script. No sample failed in either arm. The Gemini tool errors are git and node checks the models ran outside a repository, alike in both arms.

settings.effort: each route's effort is in routes: medium by default, DeepSeek high (it has no medium), and an EVAL_MODELS @<effort> replaces either

regressionRule: all tasks, per model: total tokens with the 95% interval above zero; requests up more than 10% with the 95% interval above zero; failures +2 or more; any tool-error increase
